rulings.decision: Preserve the exact resolution outcome enum; add a separate usage_outcome column for USAGE codes (USED, NOT_USED, REFUSED or the guided ledger outcome). RELEASE forbids usage_outcome; USAGE requires it. Neither column stores a value.
rulings.oracle: C-11 distinguishes declared-but-unreached from typed secrets; SEC-9 scans values and proves append-only.

rulings.decision: Digest the canonical dispatch body after removing the entire secret object. Independently bind the safe secret identity (secretId and sourceInputId) in the idempotency entry and compare it before returning a replay response. Values, Vault versions and origin lists never enter that entry.
rulings.oracle: C-15: rotation changes no digest; changed secretId or sourceInputId refuses with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

rulings.decision: Retain the worker revocation sweep for write-once revoked_at and audit. Deliver revocation independently through a synchronous names-only mayUse check on replay control reads/progress acknowledgements and guided claim/renewal. For secret-bearing runs/sessions, schedule control/renew requests on an absolute one-second cadence and cap each request at one second. A missed deadline fails closed by stopping locally; an explicit authorization denial stops guided runtime with REVOKED. Do not wait for a two-second sweep followed by another two-second poll. No new secret-bearing channel is added.
rulings.bound: At most one second until the next request plus one second for its response/deadline, plus one already in-flight step. Network/provider failure cannot prolong fill authority because the request deadline stops locally.
rulings.oracle: C-4 times from mayUse=false to local cancellation on guided learn and observed replay; exercises actual observed definite-refusal retry and Vault outage paths, not compile-path behavior. Sweep/audit evidence remains required.

rulings.decision: Keep publication/readiness verification pure: reject secret-token overlap, invalid provenance and literal secret uses without resolving Vault. Add a transient resolved-value check on each named verifier: ObservedRevisionVerifier.assertResolvedSecretLiterals receives the ephemeral resolution object inside ObservedReplayAuthorization.job(), and validator/observedReplay exposes the equivalent check invoked when Execute3.secrets arrives before execution. Both refuse a fill literal equal to a resolved declared secret. Neither verifier performs a Vault read, persists the values, nor retains them after the existing resolution/child lifetime.
rulings.oracle: SEC-8 mutates an artifact to a resolved canary literal and proves both named verifiers reject; token-span mutation is rejected on the pure path; resolution remains inside ordinary dispatch and artifactHash remains rotation-invariant.
rulings.poAmendment: None: both named verifiers perform the exact refusal, through explicit pure and transient entry points.

rulings.decision: Partition the audit by release_occurred_at: every USAGE row carries its RELEASE timestamp, while occurred_at records its actual event time. Keep related RELEASE/USAGE rows in the same retention month. Use an immutable insert trigger plus lock to prove the full scoped RELEASE locator; retain real session/admission/execution foreign keys. No self-FK is required by AC-14. Ordinary UPDATE/DELETE remains trigger-refused; the existing privileged partition-detach/drop pruner applies its existing twelve-month window. Backend adds this audit family/time-key to existing partition/bootstrap/health/retention manager allowlists.
rulings.oracle: PostgreSQL migration/retention test proves wrong scope/locator refusal, ordinary UPDATE/DELETE refusal, cross-month USAGE release-month alignment and detach/drop pruning using the existing retention window.
rulings.qualification: Root explicitly accepted this design after considering self-FK detach complexity; tests must prove the immutable scoped join and partition retention without claiming a foreign key exists.

rulings.decision: RELEASE means a release authorization decision, including zero-send refusals. Normal decisions carry decision_stage DISPATCH. Mid-run revocation appends a new RELEASE event with decision_stage LIVE_RECHECK and outcome REVOKED_MID_RUN, affected_release_id pointing to the prior RESOLVED release and its unchanged release_occurred_at. A full identity trigger proves scope/attempt/secret/coordinate; unique affected release+retention key prevents repeat. This event causes no send, no new release sequence and no additional terminal USAGE summary. Existing rows are never overwritten.
rulings.unreachedSecret: A declared but unreached guided secret has never been resolved: append terminal USAGE NOT_USED with null release_id, admission_id and vault_version, declaring coordinate and session/attempt identity; release_occurred_at equals its own occurred_at solely for retention. This is the only unlinked usage variant. All other usage summaries require the scoped actual RELEASE. Do not fabricate a RELEASE or read Vault to satisfy an audit relationship. Resolution outcome is null only in this unlinked NOT_USED variant because no resolution decision occurred; every actual RELEASE and linked USAGE requires a nonnull member of the exact outcome enum. Null means absence, never an added outcome code.
rulings.oracle: C-11 proves exactly one usage summary per declared secret including no-release NOT_USED; C-4 proves one unique live-recheck revocation event, no extra send, correct scoped linkage and immutable earlier usage.
rulings.schema: row_kind remains RELEASE|USAGE; exact resolution outcome enum unchanged; decision_stage and affected_release_id carry safe structural event metadata only.
rulings.poAmendment: Pending narrow independent PO delta: AC-14 outcome enum wording needs explicit null absence for unreached NOT_USED. Root owns amendment/revalidation; no GO claim here.
